How to use it offline

Open this site directly in your browser while online. Wait for Offline ready, then install it from the button or browser menu. On iPhone/iPad use Safari → Share → Add to Home Screen. You can also reopen the saved site in the same browser without installing. Offline use includes project switching, local file imports, flux calculations, GPS matching, heatmaps and PNG/JPG exports. Installation is per device/browser; projects do not sync automatically. Export results regularly: clearing browser/site storage or device storage eviction can remove saved app files and projects. Reconnect to download updates, save any reading edits and choose Apply update.

01 / GAS RECORDING

LI-COR concentration recordings

Select one or more tab-delimited .data files, containing CO₂ (ppm), CH₄ (ppb), date and time. Additional uploads are appended. Each reading stays linked to its source recording; duplicate filenames are skipped.

02 / FIELD CONDITIONS

Field times & conditions per reading

Upload Excel (.xlsx / .xls) or CSV with point id, date, start_time, optional end_time, temperature (°C) and pressure (absolute kPa). Field-condition time is the source of truth for the measurement timeline. The matched .data remark period supplies concentration samples and elapsed measurement duration. The analyser’s clock may differ by any amount: matching uses project, reading ID and optional source_file, never clock proximity. Repeated IDs stay separate: each occurrence is its own closure, flux and R². No occurrence column is needed. Repeated IDs are matched automatically: field rows are ordered by their date/time, then paired with separate chronological .data remark periods. If times are unavailable, spreadsheet row order is used. Optional source_file limits matching to a particular recording. You can review the assigned measurement and source in the register.

03 / LOCATION

GPS coordinates for each reading

Upload a time-stamped GPS track (including your Location.csv): no point IDs are needed. The app finds stationary periods and matches them to the field-condition measurement times. It uses median coordinates from overlapping GPS fixes. ID-based Excel/CSV or GeoJSON points are also supported. Estimated matches and unmatched readings appear in the GPS report.

Upload GPS coordinates and calculate readings to generate a heatmap.

Built for a manual closed loop

Flux = slope × P × V / (R × T × A). CO₂ slopes use ppm/s and return µmol m⁻² s⁻¹; CH₄ slopes use ppb/s and return nmol m⁻² s⁻¹. Pressure is converted from kPa to Pa, temperature from °C to K, and volume from litres to m³. Positive flux indicates emission; negative indicates uptake.

Use chamber air temperature and absolute chamber/ambient pressure. CAVITY_T and CAVITY_P describe the analyser and are never auto-filled here. Imported concentrations are used as reported; no extra water-vapour correction is applied.
Effective volume = chamber headspace + collar headspace above the soil + tubing / loop dead volume. Do not include the buried collar volume. Soil area is the collar’s internal cross-sectional area.

Select closure start and end times, then exclude an initial mixing period. Review the trace and R² for leaks, curvature and unstable fits. Remark periods suggest closure windows, using the first and last marked sample. Same-label periods separated by at most 2 seconds are merged and flagged. Short or repeated labels need review. The field-condition clock places readings on the timeline; .data remarks supply samples and duration. Clock offsets do not affect matching or the concentration slope. Actual windows can be adjusted manually when needed. This version uses ordinary linear regression and does not fit nonlinear chamber models. Data stays in this browser in IndexedDB; export results for backup. Multiple recording uploads are appended, with each reading calculated only from its source file. The heatmap uses a local metre-based layout from GPS coordinates and requires no map tiles. The default spatial view shows flux-coloured measurement points and separate GPS uncertainty rings. Optional heatmap smoothing uses normalized flux means; colour never encodes sample count or opacity. Use field-time filters for comparable visits. Blank ground is not measured zero flux; the surface is exploratory, not a validated model of unsampled ground.
